cardH3_damageCensus.rootCauseSummary: src/jobs/parcel-record-fill.mjs's instantiateAndIngest()/upsertRecords() generates a default cell for EVERY declared rail (via the vendored engine's instantiateParcelRecord) and unconditionally upserts ALL of them via UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL (ON CONFLICT (place_key, rail_key) DO UPDATE SET cell_state = EXCLUDED.cell_state), with no filter for rails this job does not itself populate. Every rail whose real data comes from a SEPARATE specialized job (flood-ingest.mjs, parcel-r4-companions.mjs for wells/specialDistricts, parcel-value-history.mjs, parcel-r5-zoning.mjs) gets silently overwritten back to the engine's default 'unaccounted' state EVERY TIME parcel-record-fill runs for that county, for ANY reason -- including runs whose actual purpose is unrelated (e.g. verifying a dollar-rail crosswalk fix). Code-verified by reading the upsert path directly (see CP2), not inferred from timing alone.

whatContradictedTheCard: The card's own premise ('Idempotent re-runs; ... deltas reported verbatim per county', 'Expect ~1% magnitude; a much larger delta is a finding') anticipated a SMALL delta from the fragment-union fix specifically. The actual live state contradicts the premise that there was a stable baseline to diff against at all: the baseline itself had been silently destroyed by an unrelated defect (parcel-record-fill's non-owned-rail clobber) hours to minutes before this card ran step 2's premise-check. Running step 2 as originally scoped would have reported a delta that looked like validation of the fragment-union fix but was actually mostly measuring damage from a different bug -- exactly the kind of misleading close the queue protocol's contradiction-reporting rule exists to catch.

Two mechanisms were considered for the reset before settling on parcel-record-fill: PARCEL-S6-COLLISION's remediation (rejected: its own dispatch scopes any reset to 777 accounts' dollar cells specifically, three orders of magnitude smaller than the ~900K+ cells actually affected, and the runs-table evidence points at ordinary parcel-record-fill phase executions, not an S6-specific phase) and, per the operator's own correction mid-card, the possibility that the current in-flight Williamson run WAS S6-COLLISION-related verification traffic (plausible and not excluded -- S6-COLLISION may be the reason Williamson specifically has had far more parcel-record-fill invocations today than any other county) even though the clobber MECHANISM itself is a parcel-record-fill defect, not an S6-COLLISION-authored one.

LESSON: A recovered lapsed lane's own diagnostic scratch scripts are worth reading in full before writing new ones -- this card's baseline-discrepancy discovery, the runs-table correlation, and the wipe-scope census all reused or lightly adapted five scripts a prior, un-closed claim on this same card had already written.

When a combined multi-condition query times out under store load, splitting into narrower per-condition queries (here, per rail_key instead of rail_key = ANY(array)) is often both cheaper AND more informative -- it turns one all-or-nothing failure into six independent, individually-timed results, some of which succeed even when the combined form does not.

A code-level defect that produces a large, confusing store-state discrepancy is worth pausing an in-progress card for, even when the card's own narrow deliverable (here, PR #71) is already done and clean -- reporting the discrepancy as a footnote in an otherwise-successful close would have buried a board-wide finding inside a small card's paperwork.
